findings.text: She never saw the arrow go. She heard it, a hard flat smack, a shutter slammed in a wind.
findings.deletionTest: She heard it, a hard flat smack, a shutter slammed in a wind.
findings.reason: Pattern 5. It says what she did not do (see the arrow) before what she did (hear it). The speed fact fits in one positive sentence. None of the four keep conditions applies: no in-scene decision turns on it, it corrects no placement, and it sets no world rule.
findings.suggestedFix: She only heard the arrow, a hard flat smack, a shutter slammed in a wind.
findings.fixNote: L653 'Jaina hadn't seen her cross it either.' still reads correctly, because 'only heard' implies she did not see the arrow. Uses a comma, not a colon, because punct_colon_narration is already at its cap of 17.

audits.dominantPattern: Pattern 10 - receiver noun with perception verb
audits.secondSweep: Re-read every sentence for an inanimate or abstract subject carrying a verb of agency, desire, cognition, combustion or physical behaviour. Roads and geography: 'the lane turned between two cottages' (L5) and 'One way went back north' (L1025) are spatial-route verbs, the same family as 'the road led'. Receiver nouns: 'the street could see it' (L605) is the one live smear. 'a whole lane drew one bucket' (L380) and 'every house ... sitting down to its dinner' (L258, L282) are household metonymy, and the residents are named on Tobin's slate. Body-part subjects: Brask's thumb (L74, L78, L98, L715, L825, L845) is his involuntary tell, read on purpose and paid off at L845. Other body-part subjects are reflex or collapse: L298, L304, L643, L685 'of their own accord', L723, L789 heels, L793 teeth. Abstract states settling into the body: 'Old copper sat on the back of her tongue' (L1) and 'the cold sat under her breastbone' (L11) use stative verbs with no landing or settling motion. The cold climbing the staff (L200, L294, L585, L665, L685) is the established frost-cost mechanic. Metaphor chains: the staff and crystal (ticked, woke, shifted and leaning) is the focus's defined reactive behaviour, carried in from the Ch3 close where it points south. Only L605 failed the sweep.

findings.text: She said a word she had learned from the gunners, and Lyriel's mouth twitched.
findings.reason: Second near-smile mouth beat in the chapter (L554 Sylvanas 'One corner of her mouth went in' is the first and survives, since it is character-specific for Sylvanas's restraint). findings.text: Brask stood in the door a moment longer, looking at the boy.
